title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention
author: Asha Menon
description: This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve request queueing fairness and prevent starvation for low-volume/long-latency requests. Motivation: experiments on the staged load test showed a recurring p99 latency regression for priority=low requests when high-throughput streams dominated the batcher, attributed to queue head-of-line blocking and unbounded wait accumulation. Changes include: (1) a priority aging mechanism that increases effective priority for requests that exceed an aging threshold, (2) configurable per-priority max_queue_wait_ms and starvation_threshold_ms, (3) soft preemption to allow a small percentage of reserved batch slots for aged requests, (4) tighter integration with KV cache to avoid inflating batching windows for cached prefix hits, and (5) added scheduler-level metrics and alerts for queue depth, age histogram and fairness_ratio. Backward-compatible: all configs default to previous behavior. Rollout: canary enabled on Dedicated pool in us-west-2 then global rollout with automatic rollback if fairness_ratio < 0.9 or p99 increases > 3%.

release_notes: Improves continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and prevents starvation for low-volume/long-wait requests by introducing priority aging, configurable queue wait/timeouts, and soft preemption. Includes new metrics and runbook updates. Backward-compatible defaults.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: potential increase in average latency for high-throughput streams due to reserved slots for aged requests. Mitigation: soft preemption with tunable reservation fraction and canary rollout with automatic rollback thresholds; observability added to monitor fairness_ratio and p99 changes.
manual_steps: To tune in production: update service/continuous_batcher/config.yaml with max_queue_wait_ms and starvation_threshold_ms, set reservation_fraction, and deploy canary to a dedicated pool. See docs/operational/runbooks/continuous-batcher.md.
